title: Platform-wide slowness and 429s
executive_summary: INC-011 (SEV2) affected api-gateway, auth-service and user-service with widespread latency and HTTP 429 errors starting around 20:00Z on 2026-10-02. Final status is ROOT_CAUSE_IDENTIFIED. The leading hypothesis (confidence 0.83) is a traffic surge at api-gateway driven by mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients retrying without honouring Retry-After. Gateway request rate stepped from a baseline of about 1195 rps to a window mean of about 2839 rps beginning 19:55Z (H1; met-api-gateway-request_rate-1930-2030). The gateway logged the mobile-ios-7.4.0 retry attribution at 19:55:11Z (logpat-api-gateway-d39f8491) and the first 429 at 19:56:06Z (logpat-api-gateway-8a499a8e). A single client reported at 1700 rps (logpat-api-gateway-8575c4f9) exceeds the pre-incident gateway baseline, which is sufficient to explain the step. The gateway rate limiter then returned 429s, and retries sustained the elevated load through about 20:25Z. Error rate rose from 0.51% to a window mean of 4.14% (max 7.6%). Auth-service and user-service load doubled at 19:55Z, consistent with being reached through the gateway. The user-service 7.1.3 release (19:48Z) was rejected as the cause (H2), and a stricter rate-limit configuration was rejected (H3). The unnamed external-driver hypothesis (H4) was rejected, though not fully excluded.

hypotheses.description: A surge of inbound traffic beginning 19:55Z, driven by mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients retrying without honouring Retry-After, roughly doubled load at api-gateway. The gateway rate limiter then returned 429s, which feed further retries. Mechanism: Client retry behaviour (mobile-ios-7.4.0, Retry-After ignored) -> request rate at api-gateway steps ~2.3x at 19:55 -> gateway CPU rises to ~65-90% and error rate steps from 0.5% to ~7% at 19:56-20:00 as the rate limiter returns 429s -> clients keep retrying, sustaining the step through 20:25. Auth-service and user-service see the same step at 19:55 because they are reached through the gateway.

critic_review.summary: H1 is the leading hypothesis and is supported by independent sources. New evidence from this round: the gateway logged "Top client by RPS: mobile-ios-7.4.0 (1700 rps)" at 19:56:19 (logpat-api-gateway-8575c4f9). That single client accounts for more than the entire pre-incident gateway baseline (~1195 rps), so it is sufficient to explain the ~1640 rps step. Timing is consistent: the gateway request_rate step begins at 19:55, the retry attribution for mobile-ios-7.4.0 appears at 19:55:11, and the first 429 at 19:56:06, followed by the error-rate step at 19:56. The auth-service doubling is also explained by this path. Auth is called only by api-gateway and payment-service (topology), and payment-service request rate is flat (+0.3%, met-payment-service-request_rate-1945-2030), so the auth step must arrive through the gateway. H2 is rejected: user-service 7.1.3 is a copy-only change, it cannot drive auth traffic (which does not depend on user-service), user-service p99 is flat, and its request step is downstream of the same gateway surge. H3 is rejected: inbound volume rose before any 429, no config changes exist in the window (get_config_changes returned none), and a stricter limiter cannot increase upstream load. H4 is largely superseded: the client-level attribution identifies a named driver, so an unnamed external source is not required, though it is not fully excluded. Residual caveats: the retry-ratio figures (314–396%) are not a valid fraction and should not be used as a volume measure; the Retry-After-ignored behaviour is reported by the gateway's own log, not verified in the client SDK; and what triggered the mobile-ios-7.4.0 client wave at 19:55 is not visible to the tools. These limit the explanation of the trigger but not the root-cause category (traffic surge from a client retry storm) or the culprit (mobile-ios-7.4.0 traffic at api-gateway).

assessments.reasoning: Named client mobile-ios-7.4.0 at 1700 rps exceeds the entire gateway baseline; onset at 19:55 precedes 429s (19:56:06) and error-rate step (19:56). Payment-service flat, so auth step comes via gateway. Caveat: retry-ratio metric validity and Retry-After handling unverified in client; trigger unknown.

7.1.3 is a copy change with no mechanism to raise callers' traffic; auth-service (no dependency on user-service) doubles at the same minute; user-service p99 flat; user-service step is downstream of the gateway surge.
Inbound request volume rises at 19:55 before any 429; no config changes in the window; a stricter limiter cannot create the upstream load increase on auth and user-service.

corrective_actions: Immediately throttle or rate-limit mobile-ios-7.4.0 traffic at api-gateway, or temporarily raise per-client limits, to break the retry loop and restore headroom (cite logpat-api-gateway-d39f8491).
Enforce Retry-After server-side at the gateway (for example, reject or delay retries that arrive before the advertised window) so that retry amplification stops while clients are updated.
Confirm that gateway CPU (peak about 93%) and auth/user-service latency return to baseline after throttling, and communicate status to affected teams.
Consider a temporary rollback or hold on mobile-ios-7.4.0 distribution or server-side feature flags for the affected client version, if throttling is insufficient.
preventive_actions: Fix the mobile-ios-7.4.0 client retry logic so that it honours Retry-After with exponential backoff and jitter. Verify this in the client SDK, since the Retry-After-ignored behaviour is currently reported from the gateway log only.
Add per-client quotas and fair-share limits at api-gateway so that a single client cannot consume more than a bounded share of capacity.
Add capacity headroom or autoscaling for api-gateway so that a roughly 2.3x step does not push CPU to 90%+.
Investigate what triggered the mobile-ios-7.4.0 client wave at 19:55Z (for example a push notification, feature rollout, or scheduled sync). This is not visible to current tools and is an open item.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on per-client request rate at api-gateway (for example, any single client_id above 2x its 7-day baseline, or above 500 rps) and on the retry share metric once it is validated as a true fraction.
Alert on api-gateway 429 rate and error rate above 1% for more than 2 minutes, and on gateway CPU above 75% sustained.
Track the mobile-ios-7.4.0 version mix and the Retry-After compliance rate in gateway logs, to confirm recovery as clients update.

conclusion: The most probable explanation for INC-011 is a client-driven traffic surge at api-gateway: mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients sent a large volume of requests and retried without honouring Retry-After. The gateway rate limiter responded with 429s, and these retries sustained the load until about 20:25Z. This is the most probable root cause, not a confirmed fact. The mechanism and culprit are supported by independent gateway logs and metrics. Remaining caveats are the unverified Retry-After behaviour in the client SDK, the untraced trigger for the 19:55Z client wave, and the invalid retry-share figures. These caveats do not change the root-cause category or culprit. Mitigation should focus on throttling the offending client and enforcing Retry-After at the gateway, followed by client and capacity fixes.
